scope.note: a project course derived from the committed P48 passable raster, not from the retail .aid racing line and not from a retail start line. It is a data layout, not a driven lap; no gate mesh, race director, lap timing or car simulation is claimed.

source.probe: probes/map-laps-aid (collision-raster project course; the retail .aid line is not read)

raster.source: P48 passable raster built from the committed collision.positions.f32.bin / collision.indices.u32.bin triangle buffer

spawn.source: the committed spawn pose in _work/map-batch/usa_sanfran_russianhill/spawn.json (layout.spawn); the course start is the raster loop station nearest this pose

algorithm.name: clearance-eroded component-boundary cycle
algorithm.erosionRule: 2-layer 8-connected erosion of the P48 passable raster; a retained cell has every cell within Chebyshev distance 2 passable, so the nearest blocked cell is at least 1.5 m away; the raster border is treated as blocked
algorithm.boundaryTrace: 8-connected Moore boundary trace of the component mask, mapped to the eroded foreground cells
algorithm.loopRule: the outer boundary of the 8-connected component of the 2-cell-eroded P48 passable raster that contains the committed spawn cell, or the component of the nearest eroded cell when the spawn cell is eroded (snap capped at 25 m); no point is hand-placed
algorithm.startRule: the closed ring is resampled at 0.25 m and rotated so station 0 is the station nearest the committed spawn; the spawn projection is recorded, not moved
algorithm.validationRule: every station is on the P48 passable raster and on the eroded mask, and its 1.68 m car band is passable perpendicular to the station's central-difference tangent; the closed loop is continuous (station spacing <= 0.5 m)

clearance.metric: the car band at every 0.25 m station, perpendicular to the station's central-difference tangent; the loop is traced on the passable raster eroded by 2 8-connected layers
clearance.bandTierReason: 1.680 m is the documented maximum car width (1.676 m) with no safety margin, the same narrow band the .aid probe tests; the 2.276 m band (car + 0.30 m margin per side) is a stronger clearance that needs a 3-cell erosion and selects a smaller component
